propositions: The reconciler unconditionally advances its cursor to the newest event in each pass, permanently excluding any candidate that failed to vote before the pass ended, even if the failure was transient.

A patch-set upload whose review times out or errors in the reconciler's first pass is never re-driven in subsequent passes because the cursor jumps past it, blocking recovery and leaving the change unvoted indefinitely.
The webhook delivery is at-most-once and lossy by design, and the reconciler—which is the only recovery mechanism—fails to re-drive abandoned candidates due to the cursor advancing unconditionally.
Manual nudges (recheck-review comment or no-op rebase) revive stalled changes by minting new events with timestamps after the cursor, re-admitting the change to the reconciler's window.
The operator cannot distinguish between 'review queued and waiting' versus 'review never queued' because queue depth and held-back candidates are not observable.
